descriptionChirho: To perceive visually, to gaze upon or observe someone or something, often with sustained attention or contemplation (the primary meaning of שׁוּר in Qal).
To watch with hostile or stealthy intent, to spy on or lie in ambush against someone, implying malicious surveillance rather than neutral observation.
To produce a song or chant, likely a variant or overlapping form related to שִׁיר (shir); attested in poetic contexts where the verb denotes musical vocalization rather than visual perception.
